summary: Closes the medium finding m9-70 and m9-73 both left open. ChronosServer::open_default_store opened the configured session store and, on any failure, logged 'Could not open session store at {path}: {cause}. Using in-memory store.' at warn level and continued with an empty in-memory store. A server pointed at a store that exists but cannot be opened - locked by a second process against one CHRONOS_DB_PATH, corrupt, permission denied - therefore started successfully, answered session_save with success, answered session_list with an empty list, and reported healthy: silent data loss behind a green health check, indistinguishable from an empty store by any client. The fix makes store opening a decision the process cannot ignore. StoreOpenError { path, cause } names the path, the cause and the opt-in in Display, exposes path()/cause() and returns the store error from Error::source(); its cause is boxed because the first clippy pass rejected a 192-byte Err variant (clippy::result_large_err) and boxing makes it 32 bytes. Three pure functions carry the policy and are unit-testable without touching the process environment: default_store_path(db_path, home) prefers CHRONOS_DB_PATH and falls back to $HOME/.local/share/chronos/sessions.redb, with empty values falling through in both cases; allow_in_memory_fallback(raw) accepts only 1/true/yes after trim and lowercasing, so a typo cannot re-enable silent degradation; open_store_at(path, allow_in_memory_fallback) returns Result<SessionStore, StoreOpenError>, creates missing parent directories, and degrades only when the caller opted in. ChronosServer::try_new() is the new entrypoint, new() panics with the same message, and crates/chronos-mcp/src/bin/chronos-mcp.rs uses try_new() and exits 2 with 'chronos-mcp: fatal: <message>' on stderr before the transport starts. The verification problem was observability: a degraded server and a healthy server answer the same MCP tools and differ only in the data, so the policy can only be observed in the process exit status. chronos-sandbox/tests/store_open_failure.rs therefore spawns the real binary with CHRONOS_DB_PATH pointing at a directory - a path that exists, so the missing-parent allowance cannot excuse it, and that can never be a redb database - and asserts exit code 2, a stderr line naming the path and the cause, and no initialize response; a second test starts the same fixture with CHRONOS_ALLOW_IN_MEMORY_FALLBACK=1 and asserts the server does serve, which shows both that the opt-in is the difference and that the fixture is genuinely unopenable. Falsification: reverting open_store_at's Err branch to the unconditional in-memory fallback fails test_open_store_at_fails_closed_instead_of_degrading_silently at server.rs:6237, and rebuilding the binary with that revert fails test_server_refuses_to_start_when_the_configured_store_cannot_be_opened with ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(256)) instead of Some(2); both restored byte-identically (cmp against the scratch backup) before the green runs. A third observation kept the cycle honest: the first acceptance run passed against a stale target/debug/chronos-mcp built before this cycle, because the sandbox resolve_mcp_path() ladder prefers the built binary over CHRONOS_MCP_PATH in the test process, and the assertion's stderr dump showed the pre-m9-75 warning; the binary was rebuilt, the run repeated, and AGENTS.md now records the hazard. Docs gained a 'When the store cannot be opened' section in the English and Spanish session-management chapters, stating the fail-closed behaviour, the exit code and the opt-in.
title: 75 fail-closed store open

subject.gap: crates/chronos-mcp/src/server.rs::open_default_store - both the production variant and the cfg(test) variant - called SessionStore::try_open(path) and, on Err, logged 'Could not open session store at {path}: {cause}. Using in-memory store.' at warn level and returned SessionStore::in_memory(). Nothing else in the process noticed the substitution: session_save wrote into a store that would be discarded, session_list answered with an empty list, and no tool reported the degraded mode, so a client could not distinguish 'your store is empty' from 'your store was ignored'. The triggering conditions are a store that exists and is locked by another process (two chronos-mcp instances sharing one $CHRONOS_DB_PATH, which the m9-73 sandbox work showed is a realistic configuration), corrupt, or unreadable through permissions - exactly the cases where the persisted data matters. Detection existed only by accident: m9-73's client_store_isolation fails if it ever runs against a fallback store, which is a sandbox test and not production behaviour, and the finding was deferred twice because the remedy is a policy decision (fail closed, keep the fallback only for a genuinely new path, or surface the degraded mode) rather than a bug fix.
subject.fix: crates/chronos-mcp/src/server.rs: pub struct StoreOpenError { path: PathBuf, cause: Box<chronos_store::StoreError> } with path(), cause(), a Display that names the path, the cause and CHRONOS_ALLOW_IN_MEMORY_FALLBACK, and Error::source() returning the store error; fn default_store_path(db_path: Option<&str>, home: Option<&str>) -> PathBuf resolving $CHRONOS_DB_PATH first and $HOME/.local/share/chronos/sessions.redb second, with empty values falling through in both cases; fn allow_in_memory_fallback(raw: Option<&str>) -> bool accepting only Some("1"|"true"|"yes") after trim and to_ascii_lowercase; fn open_store_at(path, allow_in_memory_fallback) -> Result<SessionStore, StoreOpenError> whose Err branch is fail-closed and whose allow branch logs the failure at error level before degrading; pub fn try_new() -> Result<Self, StoreOpenError> as the new constructor, with new() panicking with the error message; try_open_default_store() returning Result in both the production and the cfg(test) variants. crates/chronos-mcp/src/bin/chronos-mcp.rs: try_new(), then on Err tracing::error!, eprintln!("chronos-mcp: fatal: {e}") and std::process::exit(2) before the transport is constructed. chronos-sandbox/src/client/tools.rs: resolve_mcp_path() made public so the new suite spawns the same binary every other suite does. Tests: four unit tests in server.rs (path-resolution precedence including empty values, strictness of the opt-in across seven inputs, parent-directory creation for a path that does not exist, and a fail-closed / opt-in / differential-reopen triple against a store that is already open in-process) and a new binary-level suite chronos-sandbox/tests/store_open_failure.rs of 138 lines and 2 tests. Docs: docs/manual-ai/en/08-session-management.md and docs/manual-ai/es/08-gestion-sesiones.md each gain a 'When the store cannot be opened' section; AGENTS.md records that the bucket-C binary lookup uses the last built binary, so a stale target/debug/chronos-mcp silently tests the previous commit.
subject.evidence: Two reverts, each observed to fail and restored byte-identically. Revert 1 (unit level): open_store_at's Err arm back to the pre-m9-75 unconditional SessionStore::in_memory() -> test_open_store_at_fails_closed_instead_of_degrading_silently FAILED at server.rs:6237, the Err case returning Ok. Revert 2 (binary level): same edit plus cargo build --bin chronos-mcp -> test_server_refuses_to_start_when_the_configured_store_cannot_be_opened FAILED with 'got ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(256))' (exit 1) where Some(2) is required, its captured stderr showing 'Could not open session store at ... Using in-memory store.' with the server serving until stdin closed. A third, non-revert observation: the first acceptance run was green against a stale target/debug/chronos-mcp, and only the assertion's stderr dump ('Using in-memory store.', the pre-m9-75 wording) revealed it. Post-fix: cargo test -p chronos-mcp --lib 82 passed (78 before), cargo test -p chronos-store --lib 74 passed, T3 all green including chronos-native serial 101 passed, T4-smoke store_open_failure 2/2 + client_store_isolation 3/3 + e2e_connectivity 1/1 + session_persistence 4/4.

deferred.note: New and deliberately deferred. With CHRONOS_ALLOW_IN_MEMORY_FALLBACK=1 the server behaves exactly as before except for an error-level log line: no MCP response mentions the degraded mode, so a client that opted in still cannot tell from a session_save or session_list payload that nothing is being persisted. The closed finding was about the silent part of the fallback, and refusing to start removes that silence for the default configuration; surfacing the mode in tool responses (a field on the session tools' envelope, or a capabilities flag) changes an API shape with callers to update, and the opt-in path is not one a user reaches by accident. Not attempted in a policy-fix cycle.
deferred.severity_rationale: Requires an explicit opt-in to reach, and the operator who sets it has accepted that nothing is persisted; no silent loss remains without it.
